text:
marco: Quick alert from onboarding: bringing up nebula-50k-int2 with full prefetch+scaled-rope LUT. Repro harness shows periodic micro-regressions in generation continuity at irregular intervals: ~6.4k, ~12.8k, ~19.2k, but not exact power-of-two boundaries.

anya: can you paste the tiny repro and cache stats? I'll spin up a short canary run.

marco: repro (bash):
```bash
for L in 6200 6400 12800 19200 25600; do
  curl -s -X POST https://canary.redwood/api/v1/generate -d '{"model":"nebula-50k-int2","input":"Y'$L'","max_tokens":40,"prefetch_kv":true,"prefetch_stride":4}' | jq -r '.cache_stats + {pos:$L}' ;
done
```
cache shows `miss_band` spike at 6400 and 19200, handshake_misaligned increments around 6400 only. generation shows short 2-3 token repeats at those bins.

drew: those offsets look like multiples of 6400 which is suspiciously LCM-ish for our LUT resolution (320) and shard_tile (20) -> gcd=20, lcm maybe 320*20/gcd... I want to run a quick numeric alignment check.

marco: I dumped a slice of rotor->slot mapping:
```
# token_idx -> rot_block, slot_base, kv_idx
6398 -> (15, 398, 5118)
6399 -> (15, 399, 5119)
6400 -> (16, 0, 5120)   <-- expected kv_idx wrap to 0 but we see 5120 in some traces
6401 -> (16, 1, 0)
```

anya: that indicates the slot_base calc is inconsistent between the RoPE thread and the prefetch writer. floating LUT rounding differences could make two adjacent token_idx map to the same slot_base or leave stale writer state.

drew: hypothesis: the scaled-LUT uses a 16-bit fp approximation; different callers convert to int using different policies (floor vs trunc vs round). Small discrepancy accumulates and appears at indices that are multiples of LUT_period * tile_size -> hence periodic banding.

marco: repro check: toggled `ROPE_LUT_MODE=piecewise` vs `legacy`; piecewise reproduces banding, legacy doesn't. also `--no-prefetch` removes it. so interaction prefetch+piecewise-LUT is the culprit.

anya: suggested mitigations: (1) canonicalize rounding: add a utility fn rope_index(token_idx) that both writers use; (2) add an onboarding unit test that computes gcd(rope_lut_len, shard_tile) and warns if gcd>1 and emits candidate bad offsets; (3) add a short regression in model bring-up that runs an entropy continuity check across bins of 256 tokens and fails if a bin's top-5 overlap rises >40% over baseline.

drew: I'll prototype the canonical fn and a tiny unit test that runs over a full LCM range for nebula-50k and asserts monotonicity of kv_idx mapping; should catch these periodicities deterministically.

marco: I also captured raw pack words and saw stale writes in the ring buffer: writer occasionally reads writer_index-1 when a boundary swap happens concurrently. maybe a memory ordering/fence missing after pack buffer swap.

anya: add a lightweight memory barrier and sequence number to the ring slot header, so reader can detect stale reads and retry. low overhead, easy to QA.

drew: plan: (A) add rope_index canonicalization + memory fence fix; (B) unit test enumerating token positions across LCM and randomized phase noise seeds; (C) onboarding eval: continuity histogram + FFT-based band detector to surface periodic bands in Console. I'll PR the code and tests by EOD.

opsbot: Created deploy plan: nebula-50k-prefetch-alignment-fix (plan id: plan-20260325-42). Plan will hold until PR merges and CI passes.

marco: timeline — once PR merges I'll run an overnight full 50k sweep with prefetch_stride=4 and produce heatmap + entropy diff. if all green we'll promote to longctx pool.

anya: added a quick script to the onboarding harness that computes gcd/lcm check and warns in the model ingest log. Will put a short note in the onboarding checklist.

drew: one more: include a small fuzz harness in CI that picks random LUT scales and shard tiles and runs the LCM test; caught two previous regressions in canary.

marco: awesome. thanks team. I'll upload traces and a short annotated heatmap after the overnight run. :rocket:
